contract: Two mounts share the id w-pipeline (one widget folder, two modes), distinguished by data-mode="what" | "why". kit/widget.js's Didactician.widget() only initialises the FIRST matching mount, so index.js must init each mount itself (e.g. document.querySelectorAll('[data-widget="w-pipeline"]')).

The page owns the scroll steps (prose in .d-step[data-step] beside/below each mount) and a driver in assets/page.js. On change it sets data-active-step on the mount and dispatches CustomEvent 'didactician:step' on the mount with detail { step, mode, rule, el }. Read data-active-step at init (the widget may load after the first event).
The diagram frame and its title (Diagram I / Diagram II) are outside the mount; draw only the strip, card and overlays inside it.

Tokens: role colours are --role-agent (ink), --role-script (= --c1, Prussian blue), --role-human (= --c2 = --accent, vermilion). Engraving stroke width is var(--stroke) (thicker in the dark chalkboard theme). --hatch is a ready-made hatching colour; --grid-line is the graph-paper ruling for specimen cards. Fonts: --font-serif, --font-mono; --font-display only at ≥ 24px.

Stage kinds as in the skill README: Intake, Research, Plan, Build, Review = agent (rectangle); Gate = script (hexagon); You approve, Deliver = human (rounded pill). Step 0 prose says: 'rectangles are agents, the hexagon is a script, and the rounded stages are where you come in.'

Diagram III in s-04 draws the same 8 stages with these artifact names: brief.md, facts.md, learning-plan.md, decisions.md, site/, page-round-N.json, findings.md, log.md. Keep the card headers consistent with them.

size.desktop: ≥ 900px: the mount is .d-wide (max 960px); a 2-column grid of 7 cards, each ~220–320px tall (about 1000–1150px in all); the page reserves min-height 1100px
size.mobile: < 900px: one column, full width (≥ 300px at 360); each card ≤ 360px tall, 44px touch targets, slider thumb ≥ 44px; the page reserves min-height 1800px, so the widget should come close to 7 × ~300px plus gaps and not much less

contract: One mount, one widget, no scroll steps: the page does not drive it (no data-active-step, no didactician:step events). Each specimen is independent and works in any order. kit/widget.js's Didactician.widget('w-blocks', init) is enough.

The page owns the section's prose before the widget (s-05 opening), Problem 3 (k-05) and the 'beyond these blocks' paragraphs after it. The mount is empty: draw 7 specimen cards inside it and nothing else (no section heading, no k-05).

Each card: a small-caps head 'Specimen N · Name', the working example, and its one-line load reason directly under it. All examples use the § 4 line `total = sum(x for x in values if x > 0)` with values = [3, -1, 4, 0], or the pipeline (its eight stages, brief.md, handoff prompts, reviewers). No new subject matter. See the plan's w-blocks entry for the exact seven specimens, their prompts, options and reasons.

Every disclosure shows an arrow and an action label (e.g. '▸ Show what's in a handoff prompt'); nothing is hover-only; every control is keyboard-operable with 44px targets; reveals and feedback appear in place without moving the page; aria-live on each reveal. Reduced motion respected.

Wording of the load-reason lines: they restate directives from the skill's references (learning-science-patterns, cognitive-design-patterns, widgets), which are not evidence. State them as what the design does, not as proven effects: avoid 'is what sticks' or 'beats' as certainties, and if ICAP is named, say its authors frame it as a hypothesis (c-12; review finding A-02).

Say 'diagram', never the older word for a framed figure (H-17); call larger figures 'Diagram I / II / III'. Diagram III is the full-size version of specimen 6 and Diagrams I and II of specimen 5. Live-LLM (Socratic, Feynman-style) elements are not built or mocked (I2); the page describes them in prose.

Tokens: --role-agent, --role-script, --role-human, --accent, --stroke, --hatch, --grid-line (graph-paper ruling for specimen cards, never behind text), --font-serif, --font-mono; --font-display only at ≥ 24px. Cards are flat, 2px corners at most, hairline border, no soft shadows. Scope all CSS under [data-widget="w-blocks"].
